#### List:

- Intro
- Parenchymal effects
- Neurovascular and pressure effects

#### Intro:

+--------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| CO~2~                          | - Colourless, odourless gas                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                | - Product of Krebs cycle in mitochondrial matrix, aerobic respiration                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
+--------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Normal CO~2~ concentrations    | - Inspired: 0.04% = 0.027mmHg                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|                                | - Expired: 4% = 27mmHg                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
+--------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

|                                | \                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|                                |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|                                | 1.  PACO~2~ = PiCO~2~ + output/alveolar ventilation; hence ↑PiCO~2~ → ↑PACO~2~ (alveolar air equation)                                                                                                                                                                         |
|                                | 2.  highly lipid soluble, rapid equilibration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|                                | 3.  CO~2~ + H~2~O \<-\> H~2~CO3 \<-\> H^+^ + HCO~3~^-^. CO~2~ highly lipid soluble; diffuses across BBB, ↑ECF and ICF \[H^+^\]                                                                                                                                                 |

|                                | \                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|                                |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
|                                | 1.  PAO~2~ = PiO~2~ – PaCO~2~/0.8 (where PaCO~2~ ≈ PACO~2~)                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                | 2.  ↓Partial pressure gradient for transfer into pulmonary capillaries                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

#### Parenchymal effects:

+---------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| CNS neurons                           | - ↑PaCO~2~ → ↑brain ICF \[H+\]                                                                                                             |
|                                       |   - PaCO~2~ 60-80mmHg: sedation                                                                                                            |
|                                       |   - PaCO~2~ \>80mmHg: coma, apnoea                                                                                                         |
|                                       |   - Normalisation of brain ICF pH occurs over \~6 hours (↑HCO~3~^-^ influx?)                                                               |
|                                       | - ↓PaO~2~ → CNS ischaemia                                                                                                                  |
+---------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Chemoreceptors and respiratory centre | - CO~2~ diffuses into central chemoreceptors in ventral medulla → ↑\[H^+^\] → ↑afferent to respiratory centre → ↑RR, TV                    |
|                                       | - CO2 stimulates peripheral chemoreceptors directly                                                                                        |
|                                       | - MV↑2-3L/min per +1mmHg PaCO~2~                                                                                                           |
|                                       |                                                                                                                                            |
|                                       | ![](/content/exams/anzca/2009/B/14/prize-image005.jpg){fig-alt="Alveolar ventilation against arterial carbon dioxide pressure when awake"} |
|                                       |                                                                                                                                            |
|                                       | - Normal: ↑MV → ↓PaCO2 (PaCO2 = VCO~2~/V~A~ x k; PACO~2~ = PaCO~2~ at equilibrium if minimal shunt)                                        |
|                                       | - If ↑FiCO~2~: ↑MV may not ↓PaCO~2~                                                                                                        |
|                                       | - If chronic: ↑CSF or brain ECF \[HCO~3~^-^\] → normalised activity of chemoreceptors                                                      |
+---------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Sympathetic nervous system            | - CO~2~ diffuses into neurons → ↑\[H^+^\] → ↑SNS output → ↑plasma \[adrenaline\], \[noradrenaline\]                                        |
|                                       | - Clinical effects:                                                                                                                        |
|                                       |   - ↑HR, ↑BP ∝ \[H^+^\]                                                                                                                    |
|                                       |   - Arrhythmias                                                                                                                            |
|                                       |   - Bounding pulse                                                                                                                         |
+---------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#### Neurovascular and pressure effects:

+----------------------------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Sequential neurovascular effects of ↑PaCO~2~ | ↑PaCO~2~ ![](/content/exams/anzca/2009/B/14/prize-image006.jpg){fig-alt="Step 1 arrow"} ↑Brain ECF/CSF \[H^+^\] ![](/content/exams/anzca/2009/B/14/prize-image007.jpg){fig-alt="Step 2 arrow"} Vasodilatation ![](/content/exams/anzca/2009/B/14/prize-image008.jpg){fig-alt="Step 3 arrow"} ↓CVR ![](/content/exams/anzca/2009/B/14/prize-image009.jpg){fig-alt="Step 4 arrow"} ↑CBF ![](/content/exams/anzca/2009/B/14/prize-image010.jpg){fig-alt="Step 5 arrow"} ↑CBV ![](/content/exams/anzca/2009/B/14/prize-image011.jpg){fig-alt="Step 6 arrow"} ±↑ICP\ |
|                                              | \                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|                                              |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|                                              | 1.  Henderson-Hasselbalch equation: pH = 6.1 + \[HCO~3~^-^\]/PaCO~2~                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|                                              |     a.  Note CO~2~ can cross BBB, H^+^ can’t                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                              | 2.  ↑H^+^ → ↓activity of L-Ca^2+^ channel, ↑nNOs activity → ↑NO                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|                                              | 3.  Poiseuille’s law: Resistance = (8 x length x viscosity) / π x radius^4^) note power of 4                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                              | 4.  Ohm’s law: CBF = (mAP – CVP or ICP) / CVR                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|                                              | 5.  ↑Vessel radius → ↑volume                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|                                              | 6.  Monroe-Kellie doctrine: after compensation exhausted, ↑volume one intracranial substance → ↑↑ intracranial pressure                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
